sovereign_country.strategic_role: 最高信誉财富保护、私人银行合规与楚格州加密谷Web3枢纽

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Handmade Sharp-Edge Epoxy Resin Liquid Core RPG Dice Casting

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 12 November 1986; in force 13 July 1987)
Switzerland–China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (signed 10 September 1990; amended by 2013 Protocol)
Free Trade Agreement between Switzerland and China (signed 6 July 2013; in force 1 July 2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act of 10 October 1997 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 811.20), as amended; Ordinance of 3 June 2015 on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (OAMLA, SR 955.033); Swiss Code of Obligations (CO, SR 220) arts. 697i et seq., 627, 717a; Swiss Commercial Register Ordinance (SR 221.411); Federal Act on Transparency of Legal Entities and Identification of Beneficial Owners (adopted by Parliament on 22 December 2023; entry into force pending) will establish a government-only federal register of beneficial owners.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Incorporation public deed (acte constitutif / öffentliche Beurkundung) including the articles of association, board and auditor appointment, and UBO declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cantonal notary public in the filing canton
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Swiss notary is mandatory for domestic instruments; no Hague Apostille applies to the Swiss deed. The notarized deed is presented to the Swiss Commercial Register before entry.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy of every shareholder, director, and beneficial owner holding at least 25%
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority of the country of origin or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the competent authority of the issuing state (e.g., Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs or Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs); if the issuing state is not a Hague Party, Swiss consular legalization is required, and a certified translation into German, French, or Italian is mandatory.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance / certificate of good conduct for the latest five years for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Judicial or police criminal records authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Swiss consular legalization; notarized declaration where apostille is unavailable; certified translation into a Swiss national language.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial owner declaration and share-register excerpt (bearer or registered shares, as applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss notary and formation agent acting with UBO knowledge
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of the UBO and directors; maintained in the private company register and made available to the financial intermediary and competent authorities upon request; not filed publicly on Zefix.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and UBOs against SECO sanctions lists, Swiss Financial Intelligence Unit guidance, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN lists, EU sanctions transposed into Swiss law, and FATF high-risk jurisdiction lists. Enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, and source-of-funds documentation are mandatory for any PEP as defined in AMLA Art. 1bis and FINMA Circular 2020/1. A written AML/CFT compliance memo must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Names Index (https://www.zefix.ch) and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (https://www.shab.ch)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The commercial name must be written in Latin characters and may be formed in German, French, Italian, Romansh, or English. Chinese characters are not accepted in the Swiss commercial register. The legal-form element must be 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the recognized abbreviation 'AG' for German, 'Société Anonyme' or 'SA' for French/Italian. The name must be substantially distinguishable from existing names in the federal commercial register and must not be misleading as to legal form, regulated status, geography, or size of the undertaking.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of a written name refusal, the applicant must file an administrative appeal with the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority, specifying the proposed name, statutory grounds under CO arts. 950–951 and the Commercial Register Ordinance, the reasons for rejection, and any trademark coexistence consent or substituted name. A single 30-day extension may be requested before expiry if a notarized incorporation deed is already in progress. If the cantonal authority upholds the refusal, appeal may be filed with the Federal Commercial Register Authority of the Federal Office of Justice within 30 days; a further judicial appeal to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court is available only on constitutional grounds.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted as a registered seat under CO art. 49 and cantonal commercial register practice only if the service provider maintains a physical address in the filing canton, is open during business hours, displays the company sign, and accepts Swiss judicial and administrative service. For a tangible dice-casting business, a pure virtual mailbox with no Swiss operating site is insufficient for tax and commercial substance; the board's central administration and actual production or warehousing facilities must be verifiable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated 2–4% probability per company-year for a non-licensed, low-risk handicraft and online retail producer of polyhedral dice. The probability increases to approximately 10% per company-year if the company becomes VAT-registered, requests a cantonal tax ruling, or engages in epoxy-resin handling that triggers environmental or occupational-safety inspection.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary name clearance and Zefix/SHAB availability search
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Zefix operator / Swiss Federal Commercial Register information service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Federal Commercial Register Ordinance and the commercial-register information tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial authentication of the incorporation deed, articles of association, and UBO declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff (cantonal schedule; typically CHF 800–2,000 for a standard AG incorporation)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Swiss Commercial Register entry fee and SHAB publication
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration fee plus SHAB publication tariff (typically CHF 600–1,000 depending on canton and share capital)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization bundle for UBO passports, police clearances, and corporate home-registry documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the document's state of origin; Swiss embassy or consulate where consular legalization is required
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular fee schedule of the issuing state, typically USD 30–100 per document, plus courier and translation-agency charges

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO piercing, PEP, UN, OFAC, and SECO sanctions screening compliance dossier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss licensed corporate-services provider or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard pre-incorporation AML/CFT due diligence engagement, typically CHF 700–1,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of original Chinese documents and name-clearance declarations into a Swiss national language
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional fee per page, typically CHF 85–120, estimated at five to seven registry-quality pages

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / Code des obligations), Arts. 629-632 (incorporation, share capital, paid-up minimum), Art. 627 (mandatory contents of articles), Arts. 716 ff. (duties and authorization of the board of directors), Art. 552 ff.; Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV), Arts. 14-24; Federal Act on the Amendment of the Swiss Civil Code.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) at the registered office seat; federal supervision by the Bureau of the Federal Commercial Register (Eidgenössisches Handelsregisteramt, EHRA) within the Federal Department of Justice and Police.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarially certified public incorporation deed (öffentliche Urkunde), followed by the electronic application for entry in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zum Handelsregister) filed by the notary through the official portal (EasyGov.swiss / the competent cantonal commercial register portal).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The share capital (Aktienkapital) must be at least CHF 100,000, of which at least CHF 50,000 must be paid up in cash before registration; paid-up funds must be deposited in a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) in the name of the future company, and the bank's written confirmation of free disposal must be annexed to the deed; non-cash contributions (Sacheinlagen) require a licensed contribution audit report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BOARD RESOLUTION 01/2025 - [Draft AG], Zug. Adopted unanimously on [date] under Art. 716 ff. CO: 1. Share capital: The Board confirms lawful subscription of the entire CHF 100,000 share capital, divided into 100 registered shares of CHF 1,000 each; the paid-up tranche of CHF 50,000 is verified by escrow bank confirmation per Art. 632 CO. 2. Registered office: The registered office is set at [street, ZIP, Canton], Switzerland; the commercial register filing shall reflect this address. 3. Officers: [X] appointed Chair, [Y] Secretary, [Z] registered agent; two-power signature authorization approved. 4. Mandate: The Board instructs the notary to complete the public incorporation deed and commercial registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name reservation and legal-form compliance check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) through the federal ZEFIX business register portal and the cantonal electronic filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed company names electronically in the preliminary name-check application; verify against the ZEFIX database for identical or confusingly similar prior registrations; the chosen name must contain Aktiengesellschaft or the abbreviation AG and must not mislead as to the corporate purpose; obtain the formal name reservation decision (Vorentscheid), valid for 3 months.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of incorporation with company name, purpose, registered office and capital
Valid identity documents of each incorporator
Completed electronic application for preliminary name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusion or misleading character, resubmit immediately with a distinctive attribute (e.g. geographic prefix or product descriptor 'DICE'); a formal refusal may be appealed within 30 days to the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority under Arts. 29a and 30 HRegV.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial drafting, adoption of statutes, and constitutive board meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public notary (Notar / office du notaire) licensed in the canton of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage the notary to prepare and certify the statutes, minutes of the constitutive general meeting and board consents; all incorporators must appear in person or by duly authenticated power of attorney to execute the public deed; the notary verifies compliance with Arts. 627 and 629-632 CO concerning corporate purpose, capital structure and statutory content.
required_dossiers: Fully signed draft articles of incorporation
Notarial questionnaire and identification documentation
Power of attorney for representatives, where applicable
Schedule of cash contributions and, if any, schedule of non-cash contributions in kind (Sacheinlage)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defective or incomplete deed clauses are cured by formal amendment and re-execution before the same notary; disputes on notarial certification are adjudicated by the cantonal civil court under the cantonal Notarial Act (NotG), without prejudice to immediate re-execution with corrected wording.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Paid-up capital deposit and bank escrow confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank or securities firm, or Swiss PostFinance, at the registered office seat
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) in the name of the future Aktiengesellschaft for the account of the founding shareholders; transfer at least CHF 50,000 in freely available Swiss francs; obtain the bank's written irrevocable confirmation that the amount is credited and at the free disposal of the Board of Directors; deliver the confirmation to the notary for annexation to the public deed and commercial register application.
required_dossiers: Company formation account opening forms
Client due diligence / beneficial ownership declaration (AMLA requirements)
Source of funds certification and proof of origin of capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank withholds confirmation due to incomplete anti-money-laundering documentation, complete the beneficial ownership and source-of-funds declarations promptly; refusal must be in writing with reasons and may be cured through a qualified substitute institution; funds may be held at PostFinance under the same standard of confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial register filing and statutory publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Handelsregisteramt of the registered office canton through the official electronic filing portal (EasyGov.swiss and the cantonal e-handelsregister system)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the electronic application for registration (Anmeldung zum Handelsregister) with the public incorporation deed, articles, bank payment confirmation, auditor report if applicable, and the candidate list of directors and authorized signatories; the registry reviews statutory and formal compliance, issues the entry, assigns the UID/CH number, and transmits the data to the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC / Schweizerisches Handelsblatt) for mandatory publication.
required_dossiers: Public notarial deed of incorporation
Certified copies of the adopted articles of incorporation
Bank confirmation of paid-up share capital
Contribution in kind audit report, where applicable
List of board members, secretary and signatories with specimen signatures
Cantonal and federal commercial register forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the commercial register issues objections, the notary or board must reply with amendments within 10 days; an adverse final decision may be appealed to the commercial register supervisory authority pursuant to Art. 29a HRegV, and thereafter to the cantonal administrative court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication, definitive incorporation, and certified commercial register extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC / Schweizerisches Handelsblatt SHAB) and the cantonal Commercial Register Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the legal data in the SHAB publication within 2 working days of entry; obtain the certified commercial register extract (Handelsregisterauszug) and confirmation of UID/CH registration, which constitute authoritative proof of legal personality; ensure the registry simultaneously notifies the Federal Statistical Office and the Federal Tax Administration where required.
required_dossiers: Confirmation of registration entry and assigned UID number
Application for certified commercial register extract
Board resolution confirming the registered address and signatory powers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Typographical or substantive errors in the publication are cured by a rectification order from the cantonal registry at no additional fee; if a third party obstructs the entry, the company may seek a declaratory judgment before the civil court and annotate the pending proceeding in the register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax, VAT, social insurance, and municipal business clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for VAT, Cantonal Tax Administration for direct taxes, Cantonal AHV/SVA compensation office for social insurance, and municipal Gewerbeamt / building and trade authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of registration, the Board must enroll the company with the cantonal tax administration for income and capital tax apportionment; register for VAT (MWST) if annual taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000, or apply for voluntary VAT registration via the ESTV portal; register as employer with the AHV/SVA compensation office and accident insurance with SUVA; file a municipal business-operation and workplace safety declaration covering chemical agents and fire safety.
required_dossiers: Certified commercial register extract with UID number
Board resolution on authorized signatories for tax filings
AHV/SVA employer registration form
ESTV VAT registration questionnaire (eportal.estv.admin.ch)
Municipal trade, waste handling, and occupational safety declaration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filings attract administrative warnings or civil penalties under Art. 70 MWSTG but do not invalidate incorporation; plead good cause in writing for remission of any penalty; refusals of municipal operational clearance may be appealed under the cantonal administrative procedure act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No unitary federal industrial licensing authority applies to ISIC 3240 (games and toys manufacturing) for low-risk handmade hobby-tabletop accessory production; the municipal trade authority (Gewerbepolizei / office de police du commerce) of the production site handles limited operation permits, and the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) exercises general market safety oversight.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal business-operation certificate (Betriebsbewilligung / autorisation d'exploiter) where required by cantonal trade law; no statutory manufacturing concession under the federal Federal Act on Commercial Law is applicable to resin dice casting.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU), acting jointly with the environmental protection directorate of the production-site canton
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Below mandatory EIA thresholds: small-craft production is excluded from full Environmental Impact Assessment per the EIA Ordinance (UVPV) Annex; the company is subject only to registration/notification duties and basic environmental duty of care under Art. 10a of the Federal Environmental Protection Act (USG).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from epoxy resins and hardeners limited in workplace and waste air per the Federal Clean Air Ordinance (LRV), Annex 2, with required capture and abatement at the casting station; wastewater discharge to public sewer must comply with the Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV) applicable thresholds (pH 6.5-9.5, COD below municipal discharge limits, no undissolved resin particles); generated resin waste and packaging must be classified and disposed of with consignment records per the Ordinance on Waste Movements (VeVA).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cantonal fire police (Feuerpolizei) certification covering fire-extinguishing equipment and storage of flammable polymerization agents; structural load adequacy certificate for casting benches and resin storage racks; workplace occupational safety clearance by SUVA and cantonal labor inspectorate under the Federal Labor Act (ArG) and ArGV 3, including ventilation, personal protective equipment for sensitizing epoxy systems, and first-aid readiness; civil defense shelter obligations apply only above statutory gross-floor-area thresholds and are inapplicable to a small casting workshop.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC); central e-portal: www.estv.admin.ch; VAT registration and UID issuance via the central business register (Zefix) and the FTA VAT unit.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Aktiengesellschaft in the cantonal commercial register (Handelsregister) with minimum nominal capital of CHF 100,000 (at least CHF 50,000 paid up); non-resident ownership is permitted. Step 2: The commercial register office notifies the Swiss Federal Statistical Office, which issues the permanent UID business identification number in the format CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX. Step 3: Apply to the FTA VAT unit through the ESTV online VAT registration service to obtain the Swiss VAT number (the UID followed by MWST, TVA, or IVA). Step 4: A foreign entity without a Swiss registered office must apply directly to the ESTV VAT unit when Swiss-source taxable turnover arises, and must appoint a Swiss VAT representative under Art. 67 MWSTG where no Swiss place of business exists. Step 5: Cantonal and communal tax registration occurs automatically through the UID data flow; the AG must file annual Swiss federal and cantonal corporate tax returns (e.g., in the canton of Zug).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland has no US-style check-the-box or hybrid entity election; the AG is mandatorily an entity-level taxpayer for Swiss federal, cantonal, and communal corporate income tax, Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer at 35%), and Swiss VAT. Available statutory elections include: (1) VAT group election under Art. 12 MWSTG consolidating Swiss-resident group entities as a single taxable person; (2) election between treaty-based exemption and foreign tax credit for foreign permanent-establishment income; (3) optional cantonal STAF incentive elections (patent box, R&D super-deduction, notional interest deduction) where the relevant canton has enacted them; (4) participation relief for qualifying dividends and capital gains applies automatically and is not elective. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Swiss Anti-Hybrid Law (BEPS Action 2 implementation, effective 1 January 2020) operate non-electronically, denying deductions for hybrid financial instruments, hybrid transfers, and disregarded permanent establishments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / Imposta sul valore aggiunta) - federal VAT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 150,000 annual taxable turnover (effective 1 January 2025; previously CHF 100,000). Resident entrepreneurs measure worldwide turnover from taxable activities; non-resident entrepreneurs measure Swiss-source supplies. Distance-selling and e-commerce platform deemed-supplier rules may attribute VAT liability to electronic interfaces in cross-border e-commerce, and import VAT continues to apply at the Swiss border on low-value consignments.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not, as of 2025, operate a real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or mandatory digital stamping regime. E-invoicing is voluntary and must satisfy Swiss VAT content requirements under Art. 26 MWSTG; the standardised QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) is used for payment slips but is not a fiscal clearance device. VAT-relevant records, including invoices, export declarations, and proof-of-dispatch evidence, must be retained for 10 years. For export transactions, electronic customs processing via e-dec and, for EU-transit movements, NCTS/ECS is mandatory, with physical exit confirmation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods sold by the Swiss AG and physically exported from Switzerland to a foreign destination qualify for the 0% VAT rate, provided the goods leave Swiss customs territory on or before delivery and are not consumed or used in Switzerland. For online tabletop-game dice sales via Kickstarter/Stripe and PayPal, the AG must evidence export through the Swiss customs exit declaration plus independent transport documentation (post/courier tracking, bill of lading, CMR, or air waybill). Custom casting, design, and related services supplied to foreign recipients are zero-rated or outside Swiss VAT scope according to place-of-supply rules. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated exports remains fully recoverable. If export substantiation is deficient, the supply is recharacterised as domestic taxable at the standard rate and input VAT is adjusted.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (e-dec exit declaration; additional NCTS/ECS electronic transit declaration for EU-bound movements)
Bill of Lading, CMR waybill, Air Waybill, or registered post/courier shipment record with tracking evidence (e.g., DHL/PostPilot pickup confirmation)
Export confirmation / proof of physical exit (customs-stamped or electronically verified exit confirmation)

Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT credit evidence (required where trade finance or Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal settlement documentation demands proof of receipt; no Swiss exchange-control certificate is statutorily mandated)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The FTA audits export substantiation in routine and risk-based VAT reviews. If zero-rating is claimed without complete customs and transport evidence, the FTA retrospectively reassesses VAT at 8.1% on the export consideration, charges statutory default interest from the original due date, and may impose civil fines under Arts. 84, 86, and 87 MWSTG: up to four times the evaded tax for intentional evasion, up to twice the evaded tax for negligence, up to CHF 30,000 for serious procedural contraventions, and up to CHF 8,000 for minor infractions. Aggravated export-documentation fraud may trigger criminal prosecution under Art. 85 MWSTG with custodial penalties or fines up to CHF 800,000. The general assessment limitation period is five years from the end of the relevant tax period, extended to ten years in cases of evasion; directors, VAT representatives, and responsible officers may be held jointly and severally liable for the clawback and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB / Schweizerische Nationalbank), Bern and Zurich, operating under the National Bank Act of 2003 (NBG), with domestic prudential enforcement delegated to the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA). There is no separate foreign-exchange control administration; cross-border payments and FX operations are not subject to licensing, notification, or approval by any Swiss authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland has a full free-convertibility regime for both current-account and capital-account transactions. The CHF is a free-floating reserve currency; the SNB may intervene in FX markets for monetary-policy purposes, but such intervention imposes no compliance burden on SMEs. Capital inflows (equity, shareholder loans, founder contributions) and capital outflows (dividends, loan repayments, royalties, trade settlements) may be executed freely and without quota, maturity, or counterparty restrictions. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to: (i) 35% Swiss withholding tax on dividends, subject to reduction or exemption under double-taxation treaties (most relevant jurisdictions preserve a 0-5% treaty rate upon proper refund application), and (ii) AEOI/CRS information reporting for owners residing outside Switzerland; there is no capital-export prior license, no disposal notification, and no repatriation timeline. For a Swiss AG with crowdfunding and e-commerce receipts, all foreign-currency funds may be retained in USD, EUR, or any other freely convertible currency at any FINMA-regulated or foreign bank without monthly conversion obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Swiss law imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender requirement on export proceeds. The AG may keep 100% of all foreign-currency receivables (Stripe USD settlements, PayPal balances, Kickstarter payout amounts) in multi-currency bank accounts, convert them to CHF at free-market rates, or use them for direct supplier disbursements in the same currency. The only related duties are ordinary: accurate bookkeeping and VAT (MWST) records, bank-clients' source-of-funds documentation under the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA), and the general corporate duty to keep funds at the free disposal of the company.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (CHF, USD, EUR multi-currency)
Multi-Currency Treasury Account (CHF/USD/EUR/GBP) with FX execution
Private-Wealth Mandate (unsuitable for small-ticket operational flows)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate-to-High for settlement aggregation, but the AG must retain a FINMA-regulated Swiss bank as the primary treasury anchor. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, Multitude and similar e-money institutions) are permissible as auxiliary liquidity rails: they may receive Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal USD or EUR payouts, convert currency, and sweep proceeds to the Swiss operational account, provided the EMI applies AMLA-equivalent KYC and the funds are ultimately booked in Switzerland. Legal constraints: (i) a foreign EMI is not a FINMA-authorised bank and therefore cannot hold the statutory paid-in capital escrow, cannot issue the bank confirmation required for the commercial-register incorporation filing, and cannot provide CHF IBANs in the SIC clearing system; (ii) the use of an offshore EMI must be disclosed in the annual financial statements and presented to the Swiss bank during onboarding to avoid undisclosed-account flags; (iii) the Zug 'crypto valley' domiciliation address is not predatory by itself, but a offshore-EMI-heavy structure combined with a Zug registered office will trigger enhanced due diligence; the recommended pattern is a Swiss multi-currency account at UBS/ZKB/Swissquote as master account plus one Wise/Payoneer account used strictly for PSP payout concentration.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate for physical appearance. Under FINMA Circular 2016/07 and Art. 3 AMLO, a Swiss AG is identified by the official commercial-register excerpt and a UBO declaration; signatories are identified by valid passport and proof of address; video identification through an accepted qualified electronic identification (e.g., SwissID or bank-native video-identity tool) is generally accepted for remote opening. In practice, first-time onboarding with UBS, ZKB or BCV usually requires at least one director or a licensed Swiss corporate-services representative to appear in a branch or complete a video interview; remote onboarding of non-resident foreign directors is permitted but the bank may impose: a Swiss registered office with physical substance, notarised and (where requested) apostilled passport copies, a source-of-funds interview for each UBO, and a clear explanation of PSP aggregates. Directors domiciled in countries classified by the bank as high-risk will shift the mandate from remote to physical and extend the duration; planning for a 10-15 working day opening period is prudent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk or opaque UBO profile: a non-EU/non-EFTA resident ultimate beneficial owner, a PEP connection, or a founder with prior crypto-exchange activity triggers enhanced due diligence under Art. 6 AMLA.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport (notarised and legalised/apostilled if required); proof of address dated less than three months; detailed source-of-wealth statement with 12 months of personal bank statements; curriculum vitae; UBO declaration on the FINMA-standard form; commercial-register excerpt; traceable proof of the CHF 100,000+ founding capital chain; PEP declaration and, where applicable, an explanatory memorandum on the end of any public office.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unregulated crowdfunding and PSP settlement pattern: Kickstarter pledges together with Stripe/PayPal card flows are non-face-to-face and lack conventional B2B invoices, producing a chargeback/money-laundering transaction red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kickstarter campaign URL, pledge list and funding metrics; Stripe and PayPal merchant agreements, settlement summaries and payout CSV histories; refund and dispute policy; fulfilment dashboards showing order-to-delivery traceability; a 24-month cash-flow and volume forecast; an AML self-assessment confirming zero cash, zero crypto, zero unverified third-party payer flows, and annual platform throughput below CHF 100,000; standard terms of sale and invoice template.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Chemical-input sector flag: procurement of epoxy resin, hardeners and liquid-core materials may be screened as chemicals/hazardous goods distribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Manufacturer Safety Data Sheets (SDS) per CLP/GHS; Swiss Chemicals Ordinance (ChemV/ORRChim) classification and notification receipt where applicable; third-party laboratory test certificate confirming that the finished polyhedral dice are a cured solid article with no free liquid monomer; packaged-goods and small-parcel transport documentation demonstrating non-bulk end-user consignments; SUVA/employer safety registration; supplier invoices proving purchase of finished inputs only and no raw chemical resale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Brand/screening mismatch: the trade name on Kickstarter, Etsy or the trademark register differs from the AG's legal name, causing false-positive adverse-media hits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swiss IPI trademark registration certificates for the commercial brand; domain ownership records; a reconciliation memo mapping legal name, DBA/brand, and payment-rail descriptors; screenshot of the current commercial-register entry; trademark licence agreement from founder to the AG; compliance pre-clearance memo from external counsel.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) Founders remit the subscribed share capital (minimum nominal CHF 100,000, at least CHF 50,000 paid up on incorporation) via SWIFT MT103 from the founder's OECD-bank account to the AG's capital-escrow account at UBS/ZKB/BCV; (2) the remittance-information field must state 'Einzahlung Aktienkapital / Ch: Capital Contribution' together with the notary file number; no SNB approval or purpose-code licence exists, but the source of funds must be visible from the supporting bank statement; (3) the notary issues the 'Auszahlungsbeleg' and the bank confirms funds are at free disposal, both filed with the Commercial Register; (4) subsequent shareholder loans are routed by MT103 as 'Darlehen Aktionär / Shareholder Loan', documented by a written loan agreement at arm's-length interest (0% acceptable in the 0% reference-rate corridor for small loans), and recorded to avoid reclassification as hidden equity or constructive dividend.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 (or ISO 20022 pain.001 for SEPA-zone suppliers) for all raw-material, mould-tooling, packaging and freight payments to China and EU counterparties, cleared in CHF via SIX SIC Interbank Clearing, in EUR via TARGET2/SEPA, and in USD via corresponding US clearing; (ii) Irrevocable Documentary Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700, UCP 600) for large-volume epoxy-resin or mould-sourcing contracts above CHF 50,000, with the Swiss bank as issuing bank and a second advising/confirming bank in the supplier country; (iii) documentary collections (D/P and D/A) for medium-value repeat purchases; (iv) ancillary fintech rails (Wise, Payoneer, Stripe Treasury) reserved for micro-supplier disbursements under CHF 5,000 per transaction to preserve KYC proportionality; (v) domestic SIC instant payments for Swiss logistics. No FX or trade-payment approval is required; the AG must retain commercial invoices, customs declarations (SAD/ECS), bills of lading and proof of shipment for the statutory 10-year record-keeping period to withstand retrospective transaction-pattern review by the bank's compliance department.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC outright FX forward (Devisentermingeschäft) in CHF/USD, CHF/EUR and CHF/CNH with a Swiss bank counterparty under a standard SME master agreement
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in USD/CNH and USD/INR for hedging China-sourced resin and India-sourced tooling costs without requiring onshore CNY/INR accounts
FX swaps (spot-forward combinations) for bridging USD settlement inflows from Stripe/PayPal against near-term CHF operating obligations
Cross-currency swaps for tenor beyond six months, limited to the AG's confirmed order pipeline and subject to board approval
Plain-vanilla FX options (calls and puts) and single-barrier knock-in/knock-out options for tail-risk protection on large Kickstarter USD campaign conversions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: No annual return or franchise declaration — not applicable to a Swiss AG
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not applicable; Swiss Code of Obligations does not require an annual return to the Commercial Register and there is no franchise-tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not applicable; compliance is effected through the AGM, tax, VAT, and event-driven commercial register obligations below
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No delinquency or administrative strike-off can arise solely from absence of an annual-return filing under Swiss law

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit and correction of share register, board records, and minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of directors and corporate secretary at the registered office; no external filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before preparation of the ordinary AGM; good practice within 90 days after the annual balance-sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or incomplete statutory registers expose directors to civil liability, evidentiary weakness in shareholder disputes, and AML-related exposure; they do not by themselves trigger administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements approved by the ordinary general meeting (AGM) with discharge of directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records at registered office; no filing to a state agency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the annual balance-sheet date under Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 699 para. 2; for a 31 December year-end, by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may not obtain valid discharge; shareholders may apply to the court to convene the AGM; audit qualification and director liability can follow; persistent miss of statutory organization can lead to court-ordered dissolution under Art. 731b CO

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual direct federal, cantonal, and communal corporate income tax return with submitted annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration assessing federal, cantonal, and communal corporate taxes; Swiss Federal Tax Administration for federal tax supervision and disputed matters
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the deadline stated on the cantonal tax return form, generally in the spring after the tax year, with extensions commonly available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger estimated assessment, default interest of approximately 4.5% to 5% per annum, procedural fines, collection measures, and criminal tax proceedings in serious cases; no commercial register strike-off results

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT return and annual settlement (only if the AG is registered for VAT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the close of each VAT tax period; quarterly by default, with extended tax periods available for qualifying small taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Reminder fees, late-payment interest, procedural penalties up to approximately CHF 8,000, enforced collection and potential VAT assessment under audit; no administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register update declaration for any registrable change occurring during the year (directors, registered office, issued share capital, by-laws, and similar legal facts)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days of the effective date of the registrable change; there is no recurring annual commercial register filing for a Swiss AG
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Commercial Register authority may issue a compliance order with penalty warning; failure to register required legal facts may constitute an administrative contravention and, in liquidation-related contexts, may lead to ex officio dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary statutory audit is mandatory for listed companies and for any AG exceeding any two of the following thresholds in two consecutive fiscal years: balance-sheet total at least CHF 20 million; net revenue at least CHF 40 million; annual average of at least 250 full-time employees. Where an ordinary audit is not required, a limited audit is mandatory unless all shareholders unanimously waive the audit and the AG employs fewer than 10 full-time equivalents on annual average; the waiver must be renewed annually.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 957 to 963b; Swiss GAAP FER is the principal local framework for private AGs; IFRS is acceptable as a superior framework and is required where chosen as the group reporting framework. Tax accounts begin from the approved statutory accounts and are adjusted for Swiss tax valuation rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO declaration to the Swiss Commercial Register exists for a private AG. Swiss law requires the board to maintain an accurate share register at the registered office and to record each transfer of registered shares immediately. Beneficial-ownership information must be disclosed to Swiss financial intermediaries, tax authorities, and criminal-prosecution authorities upon lawful request under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act; the audit and AGM cycle serves as the annual confirmation of register integrity.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (board roster and authorized-signature records)
Minute Book (shareholders' and board meeting minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 to 2,300 per year (CHF 600 to 2,000) depending on canton and scope of registered-office and corporate-secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,300 to 8,000 for a limited statutory audit; USD 8,000 to 35,000 for a full statutory audit of a small mid-size AG; nil if the annual shareholder audit waiver is validly renewed

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal tax on after-tax profit (≈7.83% effective pre-tax); combined federal/cantonal/communal statutory range 11.7%–21.1%, Zug-focused manufacturing AG approximates 14.6%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Cantonal patent box relief (up to 90% on qualifying IP income), cantonal R&D super-deduction (typically 150% of qualifying expenditure), Notional Interest Deduction available in Zug and Zurich, participation exemption sheltering qualifying dividends and capital gains (≥10% holding), overall effective AG tax burden between 12% and 15% in low-tax cantons

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined cantonal/federal corporate tax return (Juristische Personen) filed electronically via SWIdec, eTax, or cantonal portal (e.g., TaxOnline Zug); Form 530 for federal direct tax with cantonal extension annex
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally 6 months after fiscal year-end (calendar-year taxpayers by 30 June of the following year per Art. 126 DBG); cantonal extension normally granted to 31 December

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity identifier (UID), seat, legal form (AG/SA), registered office, date of incorporation, board members
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete in the name of the Swiss AG; foreign shareholder details only required in annex for withholding tax reconciliation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full balance sheet under Swiss Code of Obligations with equity movement statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all foreign receivables, intercompany loans, and shareholdings; attach Swiss statutory accounts and consolidating schedules if relevant

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue declaration, cost of goods sold, royalty income, Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal payment processor fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify cross-border e-commerce income to foreign buyers; Switzerland taxes worldwide income, no CFC look-through applies to an AG

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of commercial profit to taxable income: add-back of federal/cantonal corporate income tax, hidden profit distributions, non-commercial expenditures
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare any deemed profit distributions to non-resident shareholders from excessive royalty payments or non-arm's-length transfer pricing

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim of participation relief on dividends and capital gains from qualifying ≥10% shareholdings
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach shareholding schedules and proof of holding period; relief prorated if participation income exceeds income from other sources

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying IP income relief (up to 90% cantonal) and 150% R&D deduction for dice prototyping tooling and epoxy chemistry development
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain functional analysis of R&D headcount; documentation must confer economic substance in Switzerland

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of available prior-year tax losses strictly limited to a 7-year carryforward window
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No carryback is permitted under Swiss law; control over changes in beneficial ownership may restrict loss utilization in certain cantons

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of dividends paid and 35% anticipatory tax payable to the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List foreign shareholders, entitled DTA rates, and TRC status; attach Form 82 refund applications for treaty-excess withholding

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cantonal capital tax based on paid-in share capital and disclosed reserves at the cantonal rate (Zug approx. 0.08-0.1%)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident equity injections are taxable as contributed capital and require documentary proof under Swiss debt-equity rules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full disclosure of cross-border related-party transactions (IP licenses, management fees, material purchases) and benchmark documentation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Swiss AG must evidence arm's-length dealings with any foreign parent or EPU in excess of materiality thresholds; insufficient documentation triggers discretionary assessment

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing disciplinary fine under VStrR up to CHF 10,000; default interest approx. 5% p.a.; discretionary assessment (Ermessensveranlagung) with surcharge up to 30% of assessed tax; intentional understatement penalty of 100%-300% of evaded tax (Art. 175 DBG) with criminal prosecution

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on every dividend distribution, payable by the distributing AG to the ESTV
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The AG withholds 35% at source; foreign shareholder must (i) obtain a tax residency certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority confirming beneficial ownership, (ii) file a Swiss refund application (Form 82/82a) through that tax authority, and (iii) furnish the dividend voucher to the ESTV; qualifying EU parent companies holding ≥25% may apply for a 0% residual rate under the Swiss-EU Parent-Subsidiary Agreement with an advance ruling from the ESTV; treaties with Germany, UK, U.S., and China commonly reduce portfolio dividends to 15% and substantial (10-20%) holdings to 0%
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% statutory Swiss withholding tax on IP royalties, but revenue-based royalties from an AG may trigger hidden profit distribution recharacterization if not arm's-length; Interest: 35% statutory withholding tax on interest arising from Swiss bank bonds, money-market paper, and funded debt instruments, not on ordinary trade credit or intercompany current-account loans; treaty rates for interest typically 0% or 10% on covered instruments

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CHF 900,000,000 group consolidated turnover (CbCR and mandatory Master File under LBBV); Local File expected for Swiss AG entities with material cross-border related-party transactions, in practice above CHF 10,000,000 per annum, per ESTV Circular 3/2007 and OECD TPG
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland applies no onshore Economic Substance Regulations comparable to offshore hubs, but treaty benefits and the participation exemption require substantive local activity; the OECD MLI principal purpose test (PPT) is incorporated into DTAs and may deny relief to shell holding or marketing AGs without local staff, office, and decision-making in Switzerland; pure domicile companies (Verwaltungsgesellschaften) must satisfy the ESTV circular on substance to retain DTA access and avoid 35% WHT exposure

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally or negligently making false or incomplete statements, concealing Kickstarter or Stripe revenue, or overstating deductible expenses for the tabletop dice manufacturing business
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty up to three times the evaded federal and cantonal tax, default interest, denial of deductions, discretionary assessment with uplift; criminal proceedings under Art. 175 and 186 DBG
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members may be prosecuted personally; willful evasion can lead to custodial sentences of up to 3 years, fines, and confiscation of ill-gotten profits

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsifying or destroying accounting records, creating fake supplier invoices for epoxy resin or overflow manufacturing, or forging shareholder records to misrepresent taxable profit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to two times the evaded tax, compulsory criminal indictment before the cantonal criminal court, publication of conviction, and withdrawal of tax privileges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face imprisonment up to 3 years, travel restriction (Ausweissperre) for foreign nationals, and joint civil liability under Art. 754 Code of Obligations for all corporate tax damages

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to deduct, declare, or transfer the 35% anticipatory tax on shareholder dividends despite payment of distributable profits to shareholders, including disguised distributions through excessive royalty or interest flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AG personally owes the full unwithheld 35% amount plus interest; late remittance surcharge of 5%, disciplinary fine up to CHF 10,000, and administrative penalty up to three times the unpaid tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors jointly and severally liable where the AG lacks assets and poor bookkeeping caused the shortfall; criminal penalty for directors who knowingly refrain from withholding under Art. 62 VStrR

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox AG with no Swiss premises, no local employee base, purely offshore board decisions, and no manufacturing substance, while actively claiming DTA dividend exemptions and participation relief
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits under the MLI principal purpose test, retroactive application of 35% withholding tax on all distributions, reclassification as abusively transparent, and refusal of the participation exemption for the relevant fiscal years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for restitution of unpaid withholding tax and civil damages; asset blocking, travel bans for foreign directors, and derivative criminal liability for complicity in abusive tax arrangements

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving unidentifiable Stripe, Kickstarter, or PayPal funds without beneficiary due diligence, or paying artisan production workers cash-in-hand without AHV/IV/EO/ALV social security contributions and tax withholding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reimbursement of omitted social security contributions with compound interest and fines up to three times the contribution arrears; per the Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG), fines up to CHF 500,000 and license restrictions, reinforced by Swiss banking secrecy waivers in due diligence breaches
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal sanctions including imprisonment up to 5 years for qualified money laundering under Art. 305bis Swiss Criminal Code, personal liability for unpaid AHV amounts, and professional disqualification orders
